rounds.original:
Max had always been a struggling musician, working multiple jobs to make ends meet while he chased his dream of making it big. One night, he fell into a deep sleep, exhausted from a long day of gigging and waiting tables. As he drifted off, he began to hum a melody that seemed to come from nowhere. The tune was catchy and upbeat, with lyrics that flowed effortlessly.

In his dream, Max heard the song play out to a packed arena, with the crowd singing along to every word. He woke up with a start, the melody still echoing in his mind. He quickly grabbed his guitar and began to play the song, committing it to paper before it slipped away.

The next day, Max recorded a demo of the song and sent it to his manager, who was skeptical at first but eventually convinced to shop it around to record labels. To Max's surprise, the song sparked a bidding war, with multiple labels clamoring to release it.

The song, titled "Electric Dreams," was released to massive fanfare. It shot to the top of the charts, with radio stations and music streaming platforms buzzing with the infectious beat. The song's music video, featuring Max performing in a packed arena, racked up millions of views on YouTube.

As "Electric Dreams" became a global phenomenon, Max found himself catapulted to stardom. He performed the song on late-night talk shows, at music festivals, and even at sold-out concerts. The song's success was unprecedented, with fans and critics alike hailing it as a modern classic. Max's dream had finally come true, and he had his subconscious to thank for it. The song that had originated in his dream had become a worldwide hit, changing his life forever.

Max had always been a struggling musician, toiling away at multiple jobs to make ends meet while he relentlessly pursued his dream of stardom. The exhaustion had begun to take its toll, but it was on one fateful night, as he succumbed to a deep sleep, that his subconscious would ultimately prove to be his salvation. As he drifted off, a melody began to take shape in his mind, its haunting refrain and poignant lyrics weaving together with an eerie sense of purpose.

In his dream, Max envisioned the song being performed in a cavernous arena, the air electric with anticipation as the crowd sang along to every word. The image was so vivid, so real, that he woke up with a start, the melody still echoing in his mind like a challenge. He quickly threw off the covers and reached for his guitar, the notes pouring out of him like a pent-up flood as he committed the song to paper.

The next day, Max recorded a demo of the song, his voice pouring out his heart and soul as he poured his emotions into the music. He sent it to his manager, Rachel, a seasoned veteran of the music industry who had seen it all. At first, she was skeptical, but as she listened to the song again, she began to sense that this might be the one. She started to shop it around to record labels, and it wasn't long before the phone started ringing.

"This is it, Max," Rachel said, her voice low and urgent over the phone. "I've got multiple labels clamoring for the rights to this song. We've got a meeting with Atlantic Records in an hour, and I think they're going to make us an offer we can't refuse."

Max's heart was racing as he waited to hear back from Rachel. The minutes ticked by like hours, and then his phone rang again. "Max, it's Rachel. Atlantic Records wants to offer you a record deal, but they're willing to go up to $500,000 to secure the rights to the song."

Max felt a rush of adrenaline as he processed the news. This was it, the moment he had been working towards for years. "Take it," he said, his voice firm and resolute.

The song, titled "Electric Dreams," was released to widespread critical acclaim, its soaring melody and introspective lyrics resonating with listeners around the world. The song's music video, featuring Max performing in a packed arena, racked up millions of views on YouTube, and the song shot to the top of the charts, dominating the airwaves and music streaming platforms.

As "Electric Dreams" became a global phenomenon, Max found himself catapulted to stardom, performing the song on live television, at sold-out concerts, and at high-profile music festivals. The song's success was unprecedented, with fans and critics alike hailing it as a modern classic. Max's dream had finally come true, but as he stood on stage, basking in the adoration of the crowd, he couldn't help but feel a sense of awe and gratitude at the unexpected turn of events that had brought him to this moment.

"I've always believed that music is a mysterious and powerful force," Max said in a rare moment of introspection. "I'm just grateful to have been a part of it, and to have had the chance to share it with the world."

premises.premise: A family must choose which one object to keep from a house they are leaving.

transcript.story:
As they wandered through the empty rooms, memories clung to every creaking floorboard. The family had lived in this house for over a decade, and now it was time to say goodbye. But in the chaos of moving, they had been forced to make a difficult decision: they could only keep one object from the house as a memento.

The children, Jack and Lily, were at odds over the old oak tree's carved wooden swing, which had been their favorite spot for lazy summer afternoons. Their parents, Mark and Sarah, had made many happy memories there too, but they knew they had to consider something that would represent the house for all of them.

Mark suggested the old grandfather clock that had ticked away in the hallway for years, but Sarah vetoed that idea, remembering how it had always seemed to tick away their time together. Lily suggested the beautiful stained-glass window from her room, but Jack pointed out that it was too big to move.

As they continued to argue, they began to realize that the object wasn't just about the memories, but about what it represented. The family had always been one of love and support, and they needed an object that embodied that.

Sarah remembered a small, intricately carved wooden box that she had used to store her children's artwork when they were young. It was tucked away in a closet, but as she pulled it out, they all saw the sentimental value. The box was worn and scratched, but it was a reminder of the countless hours they had spent together, creating and laughing.

In the end, they decided to keep the wooden box, not just as a memento of the house, but as a symbol of their love and the memories they had made together. As they closed the door on the old house for the last time, they knew they would carry a piece of it with them, no matter where life took them next.
